thread.title: Google to invest data centre and green energy in Denmark

author: Reuters
title: Google to invest data centre and green energy in Denmark
text:
FILE PHOTO: The brand logo of Alphabet Inc's Google is seen outside its office in Beijing, China August 8, 2018. REUTERS/Thomas Peter/File Photo More COPENHAGEN (Reuters) - Alphabet Inc's <GOOGL.O> Google will invest 4.5 billion Danish crowns (537.2 million pounds) in building a new data centre in Fredericia, Denmark, its Danish business said on Tuesday.
Google has also decided to actively pursue new green investment opportunities in Denmark and is evaluating a number of projects within onshore and offshore wind energy and solar energy, it said without naming any business partners.
Denmark is home to a large wind energy sector including turbine maker Vestas Wind Systems <VWS.CO> and offshore wind farm developer Orsted <ORSTED.CO>.
Google said in September it had signed a 10-year deal to buy renewable energy from three new wind farms that are being built in Finland and which will power one of its data centres.
The new data centre in Fredericia will employ 150 to 200 staff once it is completed in 2021, according to the plans.
Besides Fredericia, last year Google bought another plot in Denmark, in Aabenraa, next to a planned Apple Inc <AAPL.O> data centre. Facebook <FB.O> has also planned a data centre in Denmark.
(Reporting by Teis Jensen, Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips and Louise Heavens)
